name: David Gray
credit: No confirmed portrait sourced for this archive.
bio: David Gray (1838–1861) was a Scottish poet from Merkland, Kirkintilloch, who died in his home town aged twenty-three. His friend Robert Buchanan wrote his biography.
The poems here are taken from Arthur Quiller-Couch's anthology The Oxford Book of Victorian Verse (Clarendon Press, 1912).

poems.title: My Epitaph
poems.author: David Gray
poems.collection: The Oxford Book of Victorian Verse (1912)
poems.text:
Below lies one whose name was traced in sand:
He died, not knowing what it was to live:
Died, while the first sweet consciousness of manhood
To maiden thoughts electrified his soul,
Faint heatings in the calyx of the rose.

Bewilder'd reader, pass without a sigh
In a proud sorrow! There is life with God
In other kingdom of a sweeter air.
In Eden every flower is blown: Amen.
